episodes.title: The Deploy That Raced a Build That Hadn't Started Yet
episodes.description: Five since the last roundup: debugging a Kubernetes Dagster deploy (throttle vs OOM, Loki cardinality, runner cold-start), a secret sync that silently ate 24 keys, uv lockfile drift across a monorepo, browser codecs & HLS transcoding, and a competency-based interview method.

episodes.title: The Deploy Worked — So Why Was the Build Red?
episodes.description: Per-PR preview-env image resolution and the deploy-vs-check distinction, self-hosted CI runner cold-starts, cross-env deploy secrets (OIDC/ESO), splitting Terraform from a monorepo, LLM context/model-internals, and a personal reminder bot — the threads since the last roundup.

episodes.title: Four Rabbit Holes in One Day: Dependabot Lock Drift, a Phantom Image Tag, Self-Hosted Runners, and a Dead Dock
episodes.description: The day in four segments: Dependabot lock-file drift and how a Claude session's context window works; the three-layer per-PR image-resolution bug; ARC self-hosted runners with base+overlay and node pools; and a USB-C DisplayLink dock fix.

episodes.title: Seven Kubernetes Lessons From One Stubborn Deploy
episodes.description: Seven transferable Kubernetes lessons from one afternoon of getting services deployed and healthy: a config-key mismatch that looked like a broken container, single-node vs autoscaling capacity, coordinator vs step pods, why stuck pods never auto-reap, dual-stack DNS on IPv4-only pods, requests vs limits, and OOM observability gaps.

episodes.title: Why Your Pod Throttles at Startup: A Readiness Probe That Cost a Whole CPU
episodes.description: A deployment that kept failing for reasons unrelated to the code — a tour through how Kubernetes enforces CPU limits, the difference between request and limit, CFS throttling mechanics, load-aware gRPC health checks, and how a readiness probe quietly cost a whole CPU core. Transferable lessons for any containerised service.

episodes.title: Why a Half-Idle Node Won't Schedule a Pod — Infra Lessons from a Per-PR Environment Build
episodes.description: Six transferable infra lessons: Kubernetes scheduling by requests (not usage), autoscaler node-pool CPU budgets, GitHub Actions trigger gotchas, a self-erasing secrets pipeline, split-horizon VPN DNS, and shared-vs-ephemeral environment design.

episodes.title: How Dependabot Really Works in CI — Two Subsystems, a Secrets Trap, and a Lockfile Bug
episodes.description: Why one routine Dependabot bump sat with five failing checks, and what each taught about how Dependabot actually behaves in CI: two separate subsystems (version vs security), GitHub starving bot PRs of secrets, a path-filter gap that hides broken lockfiles, and the uv path-dependency stale-lockfile bug — plus why we accepted the manual uv lock fix over automating it.

episodes.title: Reviewing and Fixing a Dagster-on-EKS Migration PR: Script Injection, Database Isolation, and Tests That Lie
episodes.description: A structured review of one large pull request — the AI-Eng half of moving Dagster onto new per-account EKS clusters — and the fixes it drove: blind-detection review, a GitHub Actions script-injection hole, the shared-DB migration-stamping incident and per-PR Neon isolation, an envsubst override trick, CI-gating false comfort, orphaned tests, and resolved-vs-fixed.

episodes.title: Building the Per-PR Dagster Environment — From Helm Flag to Live URL
episodes.description: How the per-PR Dagster environment went from design to a clickable URL: Helm values layering and the condition footgun, StatefulSets and the PVC helm leaves behind, the shared ALB IngressGroup, Karpenter scale-from-zero, and the three-layer fix for CI races on destructive steps.

episodes.title: Deploying Dagster to a New Cluster: Triggers, Accounts, and the Two-Owner Split
episodes.description: Moving Dagster off an old shared Kubernetes cluster onto new dedicated EKS clusters, and reshaping the CI/CD that deploys it: GitHub Actions triggers, AWS accounts and image registries, the SRE/AI-Eng ownership split, selector vs cascade deploys, YAML anchors, and an expensive env-var misconfiguration.

episodes.title: From git push to running pods — CI/CD anatomy, and the three bugs of PR 1494
episodes.description: The second half of the PR 1494 story: how a git push becomes running pods, what the deploy recipe does step by step, how container images and their tags really work, and the three genuine bugs found and fixed — a verify script that always cried wolf, a stale secret address, and a merge that produced a broken config.

episodes.title: Kubernetes, Helm, and GitOps — the foundations under your Dagster platform
episodes.description: The conceptual ground walked while taking ownership of the helm-user-code PR: what Kubernetes actually is, how Helm charts work, what ArgoCD does all day, and how the team's two-owner split architecture hangs together — the corrected, final understanding worth reinforcing.
